title: Badlands
body: The Badlands are a cracked desert of dry earth, scattered boulders and winding canyons in the southeast of Khaz Modan, reached by a chasm from Loch Modan to the north and a mountain pass from the Searing Gorge to the west. Coyotes, buzzards and restless rock elementals roam the flats, and little else lives easily here. Treasure draws visitors all the same. In the north lie the ruins of Uldaman, a vault left by the titans, and the prospectors of Ironforge and the Explorers' League who dug at its edges have been slaughtered by Stonevault troggs woken from long slumber and attacked by the Shadowforge clan of Dark Iron dwarves, who hold Angor Fortress. Dustbelcher ogres keep camps scattered across the land, and in Lethlor Ravine in the far east the black dragonflight nests above an ancient prison. At Kargath, the only Horde outpost in Khaz Modan, an expeditionary force sent by the Warchief prepares to carry the war into Blackrock Mountain.

title: Kargath
body: Kargath, named for the Shattered Hand chieftain Kargath Bladefist, stands in the northwest of the Badlands as the only Horde outpost in all of Khaz Modan. Lying so close to the Alliance-held Loch Modan, it is often cut off from Stonard, and its head scout Neeka Bloodscar sends outrunners who do not always arrive. The outpost is the headquarters of the Kargath Expeditionary Force under Warlord Goretooth, whose posted orders call for the death of Dark Iron dwarves on sight. Beside the warriors work the troll Jarkal Mossmeld, an innkeeper and a wind rider master, and a newly arrived blood elf advisor who finds the place far less civilized than he had hoped.

title: Apocryphan's Rest
body: South of Kargath, the bones of an enormous dragon lie half sunk in the hardpan, its ribs arching over the sand like the beams of a fallen hall. Nothing else remains of the creature, and the place belongs now to the scavengers. Giant buzzards circle and settle on the old bones, ridge stalkers and elder coyotes hunt the open ground, and lumbering siege golems sometimes stalk past the remains.

title: The Dustbowl
body: East of Kargath the ground drops into the Dustbowl, a wide basin of sand where lesser rock elementals tumble about the slopes. Here the gnome scholar Lotwil Veriatus has pitched his camp, choosing the place for its raw materials and its open space, ideal for testing spells that might go wrong. His assistant Lucien Tosselwrench keeps a nervous eye on him, and his mechanical servant Servo rattles off cheerful remarks about the heat. Siege golems trudge past, and a huge carrion bird called Zaricotl circles the basin in search of its next meal.

title: Mirage Flats
body: South of the Dustbowl the land opens into the Mirage Flats, a shimmering plain where heat rising from the dry earth and swirling winds play tricks on the eye and make any trail hard to follow. Elder coyotes, ridge huntresses and rock elementals roam the open sand under circling buzzards. Stranger things pass through as well: the giant Anathemus walks these flats, and the old long distance recovery unit called 7:XT is sometimes seen trundling across them.

title: Hammertoe's Digsite
body: In the north of the Badlands, not far from Uldaman, lies the excavation of the dwarf Hammertoe Grez, who worked with the Explorers' League seeking the origins of his people among the titan ruins. The Shadowforge clan fell on the site without warning and killed nearly everyone there. Their tunnelers and darkweavers still pick through the abandoned camp, and a crumpled map left in the dirt carries a last chalked message from the prospector they dragged away. The few survivors gathered at a small camp just to the south, where Prospector Ryedol plots to recover what was lost.

title: Angor Fortress
body: Angor Fortress is a Dark Iron stronghold in the northern Badlands, the base from which the Shadowforge clan organizes its digging in Uldaman. Shadowforge warriors and chanters crowd its halls alongside stone golems, and among them dwells Ambassador Infernus, an agent of Ragnaros sent to watch over the hunt for titan artifacts that might be turned against Ironforge. The dwarves have dragged others here too: the goblin Rigglefuzz was once held in the fortress to study power stones from Uldaman, and a blood elf advisor robbed on the road saw his belongings vanish behind its walls.

title: The Maker's Terrace
body: Along the northern edge of the Badlands, close beneath the ruins of Uldaman, the vault of the titans, stretches the Maker's Terrace. The ground here is rich in ore and herbs, and the Shadowforge clan has claimed it. Surveyors mark out new diggings while Dark Iron diggers and ruffians guard the work, and a hulking war golem patrols the slopes. Carved stone urns turn up in the earth here, ancient relics that the dwarves of Ironforge fear may have stirred the troggs to fury.

title: Valley of Fangs
body: The Valley of Fangs is a small valley between two great stone formations in the heart of the Badlands, its floor prowled by coyotes and cougars. A handful of outcasts have made a camp here. The goblin Rigglefuzz keeps the scavengers off with flash bombs and grills buzzard wings over his fire, Jazzrik sells blacksmithing supplies, and the smith Martek the Exiled works a forge far from anyone who might want him dead. They call themselves a bunch of old, washed-up desert dogs, and few visitors give them reason to say otherwise.

title: Camp Kosh
body: Camp Kosh is a Dustbelcher ogre camp in the northeast of the Badlands. When the dwarves fled the Uldaman excavation, they left wagons and crates of supplies abandoned along the way, and the ogres of Kosh fell on them like vultures. Among their spoils is a cart that carried the weapons and stores of Sigrun Ironhew's camp, leaving the dwarves there without food. Dustbelcher warriors and mystics guard the loot amid the stench of the camp.

title: Camp Boff
body: Camp Boff is one of the Dustbelcher ogre camps that dot the Badlands, southeast of Kargath, where ogres and brutes keep watch while coyotes and ridge huntresses prowl nearby. The nomadic mercenary band of Boss Tho'grun, which drifts between the ogre camps and is hard to track across the shimmering desert, is said to pass through here at times. Since the band betrayed the Horde, both Horde and Alliance have sent hunters here after the stolen relic it carries.

title: Camp Cagg
body: Camp Cagg sits in the southwestern Badlands, among broken hills where greater rock elementals grind across the slopes and the massive elemental Rumbler is said to roam. Dustbelcher maulers, shamans and wyrmhunters make their camp here beside the living stone, and the scholar Lotwil Veriatus has scried the elementals near them for the bracers of rock binding they carry. The camp lies on the circuit of Boss Tho'grun's wandering mercenaries, who drift from one ogre camp to the next.

title: Dustbelch Grotto
body: Dustbelch Grotto, a cave in the far southwest of the Badlands, is the main home of the Dustbelcher ogres. Ogre lords hold court here among ogre mages, maulers and shamans, and greater rock elementals lumber about the entrance. The ogres who once fought for the Horde are part of it no longer, and those of the grotto go well supplied with scrap metal. Dwarves short of materials eye the metal plates and parts the ogres carry, whispering that the old tales of siege engines in the Badlands may hold some truth.

title: Agmond's End
body: In the south of the Badlands, past Angor Fortress, lay the smallest of the Ironforge excavations, a tiny operation where Prospector Agmond, who had charge of the dwarven digs in these lands, was last known to be working. When word from him stopped coming, searchers found only his broken skeleton, picked clean, and a trail of blood across the rock where he had dragged himself from the west. Beside his hand he had scratched a name into the sandstone: Murdaloc. Stonevault troggs now hold the site, and Agmond's killer Murdaloc lurks among them. Close by, the mad hermit Theldurin the Lost has made his camp.

title: Dustwind Gulch
body: Dustwind Gulch is a wind-scoured cut in the eastern Badlands, where rabid coyotes and ridge stalkers hunt and starving buzzards wait for what they leave behind. At its edge a rear passage opens into Uldaman, and Stonevault troggs, roused from long slumber within the ruins, prowl the gulch, their seers and bashers among them. Some carry flakes of indurium, a metal of remarkable resistance to heat that is mined in its true form only deep within Uldaman.

title: Lethlor Ravine
body: In the far east of the Badlands a deep ravine cuts through the mountains, and it belongs to the black dragonflight. Scalding whelps swarm its floor and scorched guardian drakes keep watch over it. The ravine holds an older secret: the Seal of the Earth, a prison held shut by runestones set in three pillars of amethyst, opal and diamond. Within it the Dark Iron dwarves of Angor Fortress bound Blacklash and Hematus, twin lieutenants of Deathwing. Near the mouth of the ravine Thorkaf Dragoneye teaches the working of dragon scale, and warns his visitors that their stench will draw every dragon for miles.

title: Hammertoe Grez
body: Hammertoe Grez was a dwarven prospector of Ironforge who worked with Historian Karnik to uncover the lost artifacts of Uldaman. He searched the titan ruins for the origins of his people, and for the old magics that give life to golems, hoping to find them before the Dark Iron dwarves could. When the Shadowforge clan overran his digsite they carried him off to Uldaman to wring from him what he knew. Beaten and coughing, he clung to life in the ruins long enough to send his amulet, his life's work, back to Prospector Ryedol before his spirit slipped away.

title: Prospector Ryedol
body: Prospector Ryedol of the Explorers' League worked under Hammertoe Grez at the dig north of his camp and barely escaped with his life when the Shadowforge attacked. Now he waits with a few survivors at a small camp south of the site, mourning his boss and scheming to recover the camp's supplies, above all his lucky pick. He believed Hammertoe dead until a scrawled map proved otherwise, and it was his plea that sent rescuers into Uldaman. When Hammertoe's amulet came back to him instead, he swore that the old prospector's death would not be in vain.

title: Ambassador Infernus
body: Ambassador Infernus is a creature of living fire, sent by Ragnaros himself to Angor Fortress to keep watch over the Shadowforge clan as it hunts for lost artifacts in Uldaman. The Dark Iron dwarves serve the Firelord, and the ambassador makes sure their discoveries serve him too. Under his eye the Shadowforge have caused heavy losses among the dwarves of Ironforge, and the advisors of King Magni fear what weapons the artifacts might yield. The king's council has ordered him destroyed.

title: Lotwil Veriatus
body: Lotwil Veriatus is a gnome of Kharanos and a scholar of renown in the elemental sciences, who has set up camp in the Dustbowl to perfect his shackles of elemental binding. With them, he believes, mages will command elementals far mightier than any summoned before, a perfect blend of alchemy, engineering and the arcane. He is brilliant, absent-minded and forever muttering to himself, and his assistant Lucien prefers to watch from behind cover. Years ago Lotwil killed the dwarf Argelmach, who twisted his life's work toward evil ends.

title: Theldurin the Lost
body: Theldurin the Lost was once a member of the Twilight's Hammer, until he lost his mind and turned against the cult's teachings. Before he fled, he stole the Scroll of Myzrael, the means by which his former brethren hoped to free the imprisoned being they call the Lady. Now he lives in a lonely camp in the southern Badlands, gibbering to himself and fearful of a doom he dares not name, hunting for any lore that might protect the world from the things that sleep below.

title: Garek
body: Garek is a quiet agent of the Kirin Tor, sent to the Badlands by his master Krasus to end the trouble brewing in Lethlor Ravine. He keeps the exact nature of his task to himself and waits at a lonely camp in the eastern Badlands. In time he reveals his purpose: the twin dragons imprisoned beneath the Seal of the Earth cannot be trusted to stay bound, so rather than risk their release, they must be slain. Only then will the Kirin Tor stop worrying over the prisoners of Lethlor.

title: Warlord Goretooth
body: Warlord Goretooth commands the Kargath Expeditionary Force, the army sent by the Warchief to Khaz Modan to strike at the renegade Blackrock orcs and their Dark Iron allies in Blackrock Mountain. From his post at Kargath he issues bounties on the servants of the Dark Iron general Angerforge, whose forces slaughtered the 109th division of the Expeditionary Force, and orders the destruction of the masters of Blackrock Spire. He is a hard commander who tells his soldiers to move on from their losses and focus on the task at hand.

title: Martek the Exiled
body: Martek the Exiled is a smith who knows more about metal than almost anyone, living in the Valley of Fangs among a few fellow outcasts. Strangers who find him are greeted with suspicion: he assumes they have come about an axe he once forged for the Blackrock chieftain Gath'Ilzogg, or to avenge the honor of a certain Duchess Pamay, and he would rather fight than explain. Fizzle Brassbolts of the Shimmering Flats and his brother are among the few people who do not want him dead. It was Martek who proved how well indurium, a metal of the Badlands, stands up to tremendous heat.

title: Blacklash and Hematus
body: Blacklash and Hematus are twin black drakes, lieutenants of Deathwing, and allies of the Horde in the Second War, when the orcs fought alongside the Black Dragon. Few dragons fought as ferociously as these two. The Dark Iron dwarves of Angor Fortress forged the Sign of the Earth to bind them, and they were sealed in a prison in Lethlor Ravine, held by three runestones. Now the black dragonflight gathers around their prison, and those who fear their release mean to free them only to see them dead.

title: Boss Tho'grun
body: Boss Tho'grun leads a band of Dustbelcher ogre mercenaries that wanders between the ogre camps of the Badlands. The Horde of Kargath hired him to help obtain the Sign of the Earth, the key to the drake prison in Lethlor Ravine. Once the Sign was in reach, Tho'grun turned on his employers, overwhelmed them and kept it for himself. His treachery has made him a target for Horde and Alliance alike, both of whom want the Sign he carries.

title: Hammertoe and the Shadowforge
body: When the Shadowforge clan overran Hammertoe's Digsite, Prospector Ryedol believed his master slain, until a crumpled map turned up in the dirt bearing Hammertoe's chalk scrawl: he was being taken to Uldaman. Ryedol pleaded for someone to reach him before the Dark Irons learned all he knew. Rescuers found the old prospector deep in the ruins, beaten and dying. With his last strength he asked for his amulet, taken by Magregan Deepshadow, for it could lead the Shadowforge to scrolls that would let them build ever more powerful golems. Once the amulet was won back, Hammertoe sent it to Ryedol and breathed his last. Ryedol swore that the death would not be in vain and sent the amulet on to Historian Karnik in Ironforge, who had shared Hammertoe's search and would know what must be done. The blow Ironforge struck in answer belongs to the historian's own tale.
sources: quests 719, 720, 721, 722, 723, 724 descriptions and reward texts

title: The Prisoners of Lethlor
body: Two very different hunters came looking for the Sign of the Earth, the key the Dark Irons made to seal Deathwing's twin lieutenants in Lethlor Ravine. At Kargath, Gorn wanted the drakes dead to wipe out the shame of the Horde's old alliance with Deathwing, and had hired Boss Tho'grun's ogres to win the Sign, only to be betrayed. For the Alliance, the Kirin Tor agent Garek, who had heard from the stranded dwarves of Sigrun Ironhew's camp, came on the orders of Krasus, unwilling to trust the prison any longer once black dragons gathered around it and ogres had stolen its key. Whoever took the Sign from Tho'grun carried it into the ravine, drew the runestones from their pillars and broke the Seal. Blacklash and Hematus rose from their prison, and died at the hands of those who had freed them.

title: Lotwil's Shackles
body: In the Dustbowl, Lotwil Veriatus set out to build shackles of elemental binding strong enough to master a powerful elemental. He tested his spells on shards of the local rock elementals, then on great slabs and on the very bracers that bind the greater elementals, cooled his work with frost oil and fitted a gyrochronatom. One part remained: cog number five, which his assistant Lucien handed over before taking cover. Lotwil declared a groundbreaking day and summoned his elemental. It broke free at once and ran wild through the camp, and only after it was beaten down could the shackles be recovered. Lotwil sent the creature back to its home plane, and admitted the outcome was not quite what he had expected.

title: The Rise of the Machines
body: Scouts of the Kargath Expeditionary Force met strange machines in the Searing Gorge and traced them back to the Burning Steppes, perhaps to Blackrock Depths itself. Hierophant Theodora Mulvadania studied shards taken from the rock creations there and found initials etched into each: G.L.A., with a rank mark beneath. She sent a sample to Lotwil Veriatus, the elemental scholar camped east of Kargath, and the gnome went pale. The marks belonged to Argelmach, a dwarf Lotwil had killed years before for bending his work to evil. Lotwil asked for the golem lord's head and the cores of his guardians from the depths, but the head proved to be no flesh at all, only a dark iron shadow of Argelmach, and Lotwil feared another would soon take its place.

title: The Scroll of Myzrael
body: Theldurin the Lost fled the Twilight's Hammer with the Scroll of Myzrael, and the cult wanted it back. Those who tracked him to the Badlands found him babbling that the scroll was gone, torn apart by enraged elementals who now fought over its pieces. Yet if Myzrael was already gathering strength, the scroll would be needed to stop her, so the fragments were won back and Theldurin pieced them together. Then his fears turned deeper. He sent seekers into Uldaman for the Tablet of Ryun'eh, and then, by passing as his old brethren, to obtain a copy of Yagyin's Digest from cultists hidden in Ironforge or the Undercity. Theldurin pored over its truths with great hope, and greater dread of what might rise from below.

title: Agmond's Fate
body: Prospector Agmond had charge of the dwarven digs in the Badlands, and for weeks Prospector Ironband in Loch Modan had heard nothing from him. Agmond was last known at the southernmost site, a tiny operation past Angor Fortress. Searchers found Agmond's bones picked clean in the southern desert, and a bloody trail showing he had crawled there from the west. Beside his hand was scratched a single name: Murdaloc. The trogg Murdaloc and the Stonevault bonesnappers around him paid for the deed. Agmond's last report had spoken of ancient urns his diggers unearthed outside Uldaman, and Ironband feared they had roused the troggs just as his own discoveries had in Loch Modan, so the urns were gathered for study in Agmond's memory.
sources: quests 707, 738, 739, 704 descriptions and reward texts
